correctness.rationale: Write b=bρ, s=b/ρ and use y=r/b. The energy integral has prefactor √(ρ/g). On 0<y≤1, the scaled center arclength Q is comparable to y^(1/a), Q'/Q=O(1/y), and the relative difference of the scaled height factor from Q² is O(y^((a−1)/a)+s²y^(2/a)). Subtracting the reference integrand Q'/√(η²+Q²) therefore costs O(1) uniformly even as η tends to zero; the reference integral is arsinh(Q(1)/η)=log(1/η)+O(1). Outside b the relative perturbations are O(ρ r^(-(a−1)/a)), giving integrated error O(ρ b^(-(a−1)/(2a)))=O(√(ρ/g)); the omitted point-particle integral up to b is of this same order. Applying these bounds at each positive level and inverting the increasing hitting times gives compact-time uniform convergence of the clipped paths, including T=0 and T=∞. Contact holds locally since the offset curvature is at most both κ_a and 1/ρ; these bounds give Hρ κ_q=O(r^(2/a)) and v²κ_q≤g(b/ρ)². N in the proof is the magnitude of the outward support force, despite the wording ‘inward normal reaction’.
residual_risks: Only fixed a>1, c,g, and sufficiently small fixed stopping arclength are covered; not uniform as a approaches 1 or through loss of contact.

value.rationale: The result reconciles fixed-radius uniqueness with point-particle nonuniqueness using an explicit physical perturbation. It distinguishes vanishing launches selecting immediate departure, arbitrary finite delays, and remaining at rest in the limit, with an error uniform over the relevant launch speeds. Exact-rest divergence alone cannot make that distinction.
residual_risks: No probability law, robustness claim for realistic perturbations, or extension to rolling or other body shapes.
